what_it_does: This paper presents a battery-free edge sensor platform that harvests just 94.8 nanowatts of power from its environment (using energy harvesting techniques) and still runs machine learning inference with multiple sensors. The challenge is extreme: existing systems either only handle one sensor type at a time (monomodal) or use neural network accelerators that burn too much power, limiting how many devices can be deployed in a real network. This design integrates event-driven sensing—the system wakes up only when something happens, rather than constantly watching—with an ultra-low-power neural network accelerator and a mechanism to adapt the trained model when the sensor data statistics shift over time (a common problem in real deployments). The architecture enables multiple sensor nodes to collaborate by sharing results efficiently, growing the network without proportional power increases.
